summary: Describes a URN namespace created by Network Solutions for naming people and organizations, called the Personal Internet Name. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo describes a URN namespace intended to name people and organizations over time. The identifiers are opaque and are assigned and resolved by Network Solutions.

questions: what is a personal internet name
subtitle: The Network Solutions PIN namespace for persistent names of people and organizations.

tldr.problem: Some directory and authentication applications need identifiers that remain stable when email addresses, providers, or personal names change.
tldr.mechanism: The memo describes a flat, opaque PIN URN namespace assigned and resolved through Network Solutions systems.
tldr.outcome: The document records the namespace's assignment, persistence, and resolution rules; it does not establish that the service is still available today.

today: RFC 3043 is an Informational description of the Network Solutions PIN URN namespace. The unit metadata lists no update or replacement, and the RFC text describes resolution by Network Solutions.

sections.title: Why Persistent Identifiers Are Needed
sections.content:
The memo describes applications that need to distinguish people or organizations even when some associated details change. It gives examples such as email addresses, Internet providers, surnames, or DNS changing during a long customer relationship.

It presents a URN namespace as a way for applications to refer to a unique, persistent name. The namespace is intended for use beyond applications maintained by Network Solutions.
sections.plainLanguage: An organization may need to recognize the same person even after their email address changes. The memo proposes a stable identifier for that purpose.

sections.title: PIN Namespace and Assignment
sections.content:
The requested namespace identifier is pin. Its namespace-specific strings form a flat set of alphanumeric characters whose structure cannot be inferred outside Network Solutions' internal resolver.

Network Solutions assigns identifiers through its registration system and compares new identifiers with previous ones to ensure uniqueness. The memo says names are not reassigned and their binding is permanent, including after name changes, restructuring, death, or dissolution.
sections.plainLanguage: A PIN name has no public parts to decode. Network Solutions assigns unique names and does not reassign them, according to the memo.

sections.title: Resolution and Examples
sections.content:
PIN URNs are case-insensitive and are resolved by URN resolvers run by Network Solutions. The memo says resolution can return information from an electronic proxy representing the named person or organization, not the person itself.

The listed examples are explicitly not guaranteed to be real. The security section warns that resolving a PIN through another resolver is error-prone and not authoritative.
sections.plainLanguage: Network Solutions' resolver looks up a PIN and returns information about a representation of the named person or organization. The RFC warns against treating another resolver as authoritative.
